channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Sentences Handed Down to Taftish.uz Staff and Former National Security Service Officers
item.description: Uzbekistan's Military Court has sentenced Taftish.uz editorial staff and former National Security Service (DXX) officers. The outlet's head received 10 years and 6 months, a journalist 4 years and 1 month, and two other staff members and former officers over 10 years. They were accused of defamation, insult, fraud, and extortion.

item.title: Uzbekistan Prioritizes Health: Shifting Focus from Treatment to Prevention for National Development
item.description: Uzbekistan's healthcare system is prioritizing human dignity by shifting from treatment to prevention, aiming to become a center for health and longevity. The second National Program focuses on strengthening public health, promoting long and productive lives, expanding healthcare funding, popularizing medical insurance, and attracting international clinics.

item.title: China-Uzbekistan Trade Fair Opens in Tashkent, Boosting Regional Logistics and Cooperation
item.description: A "China-Uzbekistan-2026" international trade fair has opened in Tashkent. China's ambassador highlighted the potential for expanded trade and logistics via the China-Europe freight train. Promising areas include infrastructure, new energy, agriculture, innovation, culture, and tourism. Uzbekistan seeks joint projects in high-value manufacturing and technology.

item.title: Kazakhstan Declares September 25 National Day of Mourning After Naval Exercise Tragedy
item.description: Kazakhstan declared September 25 a national day of mourning following a tragedy during naval exercises in the Caspian Sea. Severe weather conditions caused 19 military personnel to be swept away by water. The death toll has now reached 12.

item.title: Kandahar Bombing Injures Eight, Kills Seven at Mirwais Hospital
item.description: Seven people killed and eight injured in a Kandahar bombing were transferred to Mirwais Hospital. Sources report the injured were construction workers and some are in critical condition. Pakistani fighter jets reportedly bombed the Sarai Mullah Sahib area, a military headquarters.

item.title: Head of Supreme Shia Council Freed from Taliban Justice Minister's Custody
item.description: Mohammad Ali Akhlaqi, head of the Supreme Shia Council, was released from the personal prison of the Taliban's Justice Minister. He and another council member were reportedly tortured and forced to pledge not to engage in political activities. Their homes were vacated.

item.title: US and Iran Explore Phased Deal to End War, Reopen Strait of Hormuz
item.description: US and Iranian negotiators are considering a phased agreement to end the war. Under the proposal, Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and the US would lift its economic blockade. Resuming free passage through the strait is a key US demand.

item.title: Rising Suicide Figures in Afghanistan Raise Serious Concerns
item.description: Multiple reports of suicide incidents from different Afghan provinces in a single day highlight a worrying trend. The true scale of the phenomenon remains unknown due to difficulties in recording and reporting, but scattered reports suggest the issue requires serious attention.

item.title: Afghanistan's Empty Seat at UN General Assembly Highlights International Isolation
item.description: For five years, Afghanistan has lacked presidential representation at the UN General Assembly, signaling its diminished standing. The Taliban regime's restrictions on women, exclusion of societal groups, and disregard for international concerns have widened the gap with the world.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Sends Condolences to Kazakhstan Over Military Deaths
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov expressed deep sorrow to Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev following a tragic incident that resulted in the deaths of military personnel during exercises in the Caspian Sea. Japarov conveyed condolences on behalf of the Kyrgyz people and offered support to the families of the deceased and recovery wishes to the injured.

item.title: Bishkek Mayor Inspects Construction Site of 24-Story Residential Complex
item.description: Bishkek Mayor Aybek Dzhunushaliev met with residents and the contractor of a 24-story residential complex under construction in the city center. Residents raised concerns about construction safety, adherence to norms, and preservation of green spaces. The mayor instructed the developer to work within the allocated territory and ensure safety.

item.title: Former Interior Minister Omurbek Suvanaliev to Run for President in 2027
item.description: Former Interior Minister Omurbek Suvanaliev announced his intention to run for president in the 2027 elections. Suvanaliev believes a strong candidate is needed to compete with the incumbent president and plans to unite opposition forces. He previously served as Interior Minister and governor of Naryn and Talas regions.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Iraq Discuss New Trade and Investment Projects
item.description: Uzbekistan's ambassador to Iraq, Ayubkhon Yunusov, met with Iraqi officials to discuss trade, transport logistics, consular cooperation, and legal frameworks. Discussions focused on expanding bilateral trade, direct business ties, and a preferential trade agreement. Both sides also reviewed preparations for the first meeting of the Joint Intergovernmental Committee on Economic and Trade Cooperation.

item.title: Education and Professions Transform in the Age of AI, Forum Discusses
item.description: A forum on 'Threats of Artificial Intelligence in Education and Employment' at ICTWEEK Uzbekistan 2026 explored how AI impacts education and the job market. Discussions covered preparing youth for future professions, in-demand skills, and educational system readiness. The event also saw the launch of the 'AWS Academy' program in 12 universities and the 'Heirs of Muhammad al-Khwarizmi' project nationwide.

item.title: Mahmoud Abbas: Israel's Gaza Violence Caused "Unprecedented Humanitarian Catastrophe"
item.description: Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas told the UN General Assembly that Israel's violence in Gaza has created an "unprecedented humanitarian catastrophe," citing killings, destruction, hunger, and displacement attempts. He described Israel's military operation as a "genocidal war" targeting Palestinian lives and future generations, affecting all necessities of life.

item.title: Khalilzad Warns of Worsening Pakistan-Afghanistan Tensions After Airstrikes
item.description: Former US envoy Zalmay Khalilzad warned that Pakistani airstrikes in Afghanistan and recent violence in Pakistan are part of a larger crisis, with no signs of improvement. He described the events as interconnected tragedies, suggesting they could escalate.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan customs officers prevent illegal import of cars from Korea
item.description: Customs officers in Kyrgyzstan have uncovered a violation of customs legislation related to the Eurasian Economic Union and the Kyrgyz Republic. The press service of the State Customs Service reported the discovery of illegal car imports from Korea.

item.title: Teenagers Describe Easy Access to Drugs and Addiction Traps
item.description: Teenagers report falling into drug addiction due to peer encouragement, economic hardship, and unemployment. Some used "Tablet K" for work, leading to dependency and addiction to substances like powder and crystal meth. Fear of treatment centers deters seeking help.

item.title: New 'Green Wave' Traffic System Reduces Travel Time by 22% in Tashkent
item.description: A new 'Green Wave' traffic system has been implemented on another road section in Tashkent, reducing travel time by 22%. This improvement was achieved by coordinating traffic lights at consecutive intersections, not by increasing speed limits.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Gavi Strengthen Partnership for Sustainable Immunization System
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Health, Damir Osmonov, participated in a high-level event in New York during the 81st UN General Assembly session. The meeting focused on strengthening the partnership between Kyrgyzstan and Gavi to ensure a sustainable immunization system.

item.title: World Food Programme Urges UN General Assembly to Address Afghanistan Crisis
item.description: The World Food Programme (WFP) is calling for the Afghanistan crisis to remain a focus during the UN General Assembly. The organization highlighted the ongoing struggles of families facing hunger and malnutrition, urging attention to their needs.

item.title: Afghanistan Freedom Front Claims Taliban Member Killed in Kabul Attack
item.description: The Afghanistan Freedom Front reported that one Taliban member was killed and two others injured during an attack on a Taliban patrol vehicle in Kabul. The incident occurred on Wednesday evening in the Dasht-e Barchi district. The group stated its forces sustained no casualties.

item.title: Smart water meters using 5G technology are being produced in Andijan
item.description: Production of smart water meters based on 5G technology has been launched at the "Andijan Technopark" in Khojaobod district. The enterprise, valued at $25 million, was built in cooperation with China's Sanchuan company with full foreign investment. The meters are produced in collaboration with Huawei, with 80% of the production processes robotized.

item.title: Lithuania suspends acceptance of labor migrants from Tajikistan
item.description: Lithuania has temporarily suspended the acceptance of applications for work or entry for citizens of Tajikistan. The reason cited is the increase in labor migrants from Central Asia. According to Indrė Gasparė, head of the Migration Department, the number of citizens from Tajikistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan arriving in Lithuania increased last year.

item.title: Kazakhstan: 19 military personnel swept away in Caspian Sea during exercises, nine dead
item.description: Kazakhstan's Defense Ministry reported that 19 military personnel were swept away by the Caspian Sea during naval exercises in the Mangystau region on September 24. Nine military personnel have been confirmed dead, and three were rescued. Search efforts continue for the remaining personnel. Severe weather conditions and strong winds are cited as causes.

item.title: Iranian Plane Forced Back to Tehran Due to US Sanctions and Turkmenistan Airspace Ban
item.description: An Iranian airliner bound for Dushanbe was forced to return to Tehran after Turkmenistan denied it permission to fly through its airspace. This incident occurred following the implementation of US sanctions against Iranian airlines, impacting flights to Tajikistan and other destinations.

item.title: Tajikistan's industrial production grew 13.8% in January-August 2026
item.description: Tajikistan's industrial production increased by 13.8% to 45.37 billion somoni in January-August 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. Manufacturing saw the largest growth at 23%, followed by electricity, gas, and steam (19.3%), and water supply (17.2%).

item.title: Israel claims Hamas finance chief killed in Gaza strike
item.description: The Israeli army announced the killing of Mohammed Abu Alwan, identified as Hamas's finance chief, in a strike in Khan Younis, southern Gaza. The army stated Alwan had managed over $330 million in funds for Hamas during the recent conflict. Hamas has not yet commented on the announcement.

item.title: New border post 'Keskanyor' to be established between Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A new border post named 'Keskanyor' will be opened on the border between Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has instructed to develop its design and begin construction within three months.

item.title: Tajikistan and Russia agree on mutual recognition of customs control results
item.description: Tajikistan and Russia signed a protocol on the mutual recognition of electronic customs control results during a CIS customs services meeting in Belarus. The agreement aims to enhance customs cooperation, expand digital technologies, and simplify procedures.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev Addresses Poverty and Unemployment in Andijan
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev expressed concern over poverty, unemployment, and migration issues in the Andijan region. He questioned how he could remain at ease in Tashkent while aware of these problems. The statement highlights the administration's focus on addressing socio-economic challenges in the region.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Open New Border Post 'Keskanyor' with Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to open the 'Keskanyor' border post, twice the size of 'Dostlik', with Kyrgyzstan. An agreement has been reached, with project development and construction to begin within three months. This aims to triple cargo volume and halve transit times. Additionally, construction of a paid Tashkent-Andijan highway is slated to start in 2027.

item.title: Tajikistan and China to Expand Cooperation in Science and Technology
item.description: Tajikistan and China held a working meeting to discuss scientific and technological cooperation, including joint initiatives within the 'One Belt, One Road' and SCO frameworks. Key areas include water resources, ecology, climate change, and digital technologies. Both sides explored possibilities for joint research projects and academic exchanges.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Provide 500,000 Soums Subsidy Per Ton of Cotton Sold on Exchange
item.description: Uzbekistan will offer a 500,000 soums subsidy per ton for cotton sold and purchased on the exchange, as announced by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. Additionally, clusters growing cotton on their land will receive 1.5 million soums per hectare. Support for exporters includes compensation for interest exceeding 5% on foreign currency loans.

item.title: Former Bishkek Deputy Mayor Azamat Kadyrov Detained Until November 20
item.description: Former Bishkek Deputy Mayor Azamat Kadyrov has been placed in pretrial detention until November 20. Kadyrov, who oversaw land use, architecture, construction, and digitalization, served as Deputy Mayor since November 2023. The specific charges against him have not yet been disclosed.

item.title: New 'Keskaner' Border Crossing Point to Open Between Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A new border crossing point, 'Keskaner,' will be established between Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan, doubling the capacity of the current 'Dustlik' crossing. This is expected to triple cargo traffic and reduce border crossing times. The project is part of efforts to expand regional transport links, including the planned China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Prime Minister Discusses Joint Venture with Geely in China
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers Chairman Adylbek Kasymaliev met with the leadership of China's Geely Auto Group in Hangzhou. The meeting focused on opening a joint venture in Kyrgyzstan. The press service of the cabinet reported the discussion.

item.title: 19 Kazakh servicemen swept away at Caspian Sea training exercise
item.description: Nineteen Kazakh servicemen were swept away during a training exercise near the Caspian Sea coast. Nine individuals have died, and three have been rescued. The incident occurred during drills on the Caspian Sea shore.

item.title: Money changer killed by unidentified gunmen in Afghanistan's Ghazni province
item.description: Local sources reported that a money changer, identified as Gulbuddin, was shot dead by unknown gunmen in the Wali Dad village of Qarabagh district, Ghazni province. The man was inside his vehicle when the attack occurred. His father reportedly works for the Taliban police headquarters in Ghazni.

item.title: Former Bishkek Vice Mayor Azamat Kadyrov Detained Until November 20
item.description: Former Bishkek Vice Mayor Azamat Kadyrov has been placed in pre-trial detention until November 20. The State Committee for National Security will hold him until the investigation concludes. The Bishkek City Court reported the decision.
